faqs.question: I brought my product with me to a different country and can't find ink for it. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Some Epson printers and ink cartridges are specific to a regional market and not sold worldwide, although the same printers are sold in the U.S. and Canada. If you have a printer sold in the U.S. or Canada, you may not be able to easily get ink cartridges for it in foreign markets.
Unfortunately, because of customs and tax regulations, the Epson E-Stores in the U.S. and Canada are unable to ship to addresses outside the U.S. and Canada.

faqs.question: I am unable to connect my product to a wireless network. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The printer does not come with built-in wireless features and does not support a wireless (or Ethernet) connection to a network router. Only a direct wired connection to the computer is supported.

faqs.question: My product makes noise after I turn it on or after it has been sitting for a while. What should I do?
faqs.answer: This is normal. It is performing routine maintenance.

faqs.question: Can the printer still print if an ink cartridge is expended or not installed?
faqs.answer: No. The printer will not operate if any cartridge is expended or removed. It's best to always have extra cartridges on hand.

faqs.question: Can the Epson ink cartridges be refilled or can I use third-party ink cartridges without voiding the warranty?
faqs.answer:
Epson does not recommend refilling or using other brands of ink cartridges.  Epson uses a permanent Micro Piezo print head that has allowed Epson to lead the industry in delivering consistent photo image quality by using variable-sized droplets.  Micro Piezo print head can also use a wider variety of inks, which has allowed Epson to introduce such ink breakthroughs as DURABrite® and Epson UltraChrome® inks that offer greatly improved humidity resistance, smudge resistance, and fade resistance.
Using refilled ink cartridges will not void the product's original warranty; however, if these products cause a failure, the repair of that failure will not be covered under warranty.

faqs.question: How do I obtain the latest product software for Windows or my Mac?
faqs.answer: You can download the latest product driver from the Downloads section of this website.

faqs.question: What security measures does Epson recommend for its network products?
faqs.answer:
To help deter unauthorized access to your product over a network, you should protect your network environment using appropriate security measures.
Security measures such as these can help deter threats such as loss of user data, use of telephone and fax lines, and other intrusions:
Enable security on your wireless LAN if your product supports a wireless connection
Enable the appropriate security on the wireless LAN you plan to use with your product. Network security, such as a network password, can deter interception of traffic over the wireless LAN. Your router may already have a default password enabled by your Internet service provider (ISP). See your ISP and router documentation for instructions on how to change the default password and better secure your network.
Connect your product only to a network protected by a firewall
Connecting your product directly to the Internet may leave it vulnerable to security threats. Instead, connect it to a router or other networking device protected by a firewall. Your router may already have a firewall set up by your Internet service provider; check with your ISP for confirmation. For best results, set up and use a private IP address for your network connection.
Change the default administrator password on your product
If your product has an option to set an administrator password, change the default administrator password to deter access by unauthorized users to personal data stored on your product, such as IDs, passwords, and contact lists. See the product's User's Guide for more information.

faqs.answer: This feature is not supported in Mac OS X. However, if your printer has a built-in automatic duplexer, auto-duplexing is supported in Mac OS X 10.6 (Snow Leopard).

faqs.question: I see the message Printer is Offline. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
Make sure the product is powered on.
Check the product control panel for any error messages and follow the instructions to solve them.  See
Check the Lights on Your Printer
.
Make sure you are choosing the correct printer when printing.  If there are multiple copies of the same printer driver, remove the ones not in use.
Make sure the USB cable is a shielded "AB" cable not more than 10 feet long.
Note:
Do not use devices that extend the length of the cable because they can interfere with signal transmission.
If you're using a USB hub with your printer, connect the printer directly to your computer.
Note:
Do not connect through a USB keyboard.  The keyboard acts like a hub and can interfere with signal transmission.
Use a different port on your computer.
If your product is networked wirelessly, make sure it is connected to the network by checking the WiFi light.  If the WiFi light is off, reconfigure the product using the control panel.

faqs.question: The color ink cartridge is expended even though I print in black only. Why does this happen?
faqs.answer:
To keep the print head clear and ready to print, the printer uses a small amount of ink from all the cartridges whenever it prints. Even if you select
Black/Grayscale
, some color ink is still being used.

faqs.answer:
When the ink replace light is on, the printer will require you to change the cartridge. You need to replace a cartridge when it's expended or it gets too old. See

faqs.answer: When an installed ink cartridge is more than six months old, you may need to replace it if you notice that your printouts don't look as good as they used to and quality doesn't improve after cleaning and aligning the print head.

faqs.question: I installed new ink cartridges and my product seems to be doing a long cleaning cycle. Is this normal?
faqs.answer:
Yes. The first time you install ink cartridges, the printer must charge its print head for a minute or so. Wait until charging finishes (the
power light stops flashing) before you turn off the printer, or it may charge improperly and use excess ink the next time you turn it on.
If the printer stops moving or making noise, but the
power light is still flashing after 5 minutes, turn off the printer. If the light is still flashing when you turn it back on, contact Epson technical support for assistance.

faqs.question: Can the Epson ink cartridges be refilled or can I use third-party ink cartridges without voiding the warranty?
faqs.answer:
Epson does not recommend refilling or using other brands of ink cartridges.  Epson uses a permanent Micro Piezo print head that has allowed Epson to lead the industry in delivering consistent photo image quality by using variable-sized droplets.  Micro Piezo print head can also use a wider variety of inks, which has allowed Epson to introduce such ink breakthroughs as DURABrite® and Epson UltraChrome® inks that offer greatly improved humidity resistance, smudge resistance, and fade resistance.
Using refilled ink cartridges will not void the product's original warranty; however, if these products cause a failure, the repair of that failure will not be covered under warranty.

faqs.answer: No. The printer will not operate if any cartridge is expended or removed. It's best to always have extra cartridges on hand.

faqs.question: I brought my product with me to a different country and can't find ink for it. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Some Epson printers and ink cartridges are specific to a regional market and not sold worldwide, although the same printers are sold in the U.S. and Canada. If you have a printer sold in the U.S. or Canada, you may not be able to easily get ink cartridges for it in foreign markets.
Unfortunately, because of customs and tax regulations, the Epson E-Stores in the U.S. and Canada are unable to ship to addresses outside the U.S. and Canada.

faqs.question: I'm having paper feed problems. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
Make sure the paper support extension is pulled up.
If paper doesn't feed, remove it from the sheet feeder. Reload it against the right edge, behind the tab, and slide the left edge guide against the paper (but not too tightly). Make sure the stack of paper is not above the arrow mark inside the edge guide.
If multiple pages feed at once, remove the paper from the sheet feeder, fan the edges to separate the sheets, then reload it.
If the paper doesn't eject fully, you may have set the wrong paper size. Press the
paper button to eject the paper. Select the correct paper size before you reprint.
If it's wrinkled when it ejects, the paper may be damp or too thin. Load new paper.
Make sure you use new, smooth, high-quality paper that is not curled, creased, old, or too thin. Load it printable side up.
Do not load hole-punched paper.
Store any unused paper flat to prevent it from curling in its original packaging in a dry area.
Heavily saturated prints may curl, causing a paper jam when you're printing on both sides of the paper.
Don't load more than the recommended number of sheets. If you're printing on both sides of the paper, try loading fewer sheets.

However, for the best results, you'll want to use one of Epson's special ink jet papers designed for your printer. See

faqs.question: Can I select a print resolution by indicating a specific dpi (dots per inch) setting?
faqs.answer:
No. The print resolution is determined by other driver software settings.
In Windows, the

and paper
Type

In Mac OS X, the resolution settings depend on the

setting:
Note:

from the pull-down menu.

Media Type
setting and the position of the Quality/Speed slider.
If you've selected
Advanced
as the
Mode
setting, the resolution is determined by the
Media Type
setting and the
Print Quality
setting.

When you change your print settings from within a program, the changes apply only while you're printing at that time in the open program. If you want to select different settings to use in all your programs, you can change the default print settings. Follow the steps below for your operating system.
Windows 2000, XP, Vista
Right-click the
printer icon in the task bar (bottom-right corner of your screen), and select
Printer Settings
.
Select the settings you want to use as defaults in all your Windows programs.
Click
OK
to accept the changes.

Print
from the File menu.

Click the
Presets
pop-up menu and do one of the following:

Last Used Settings

Save As

OK

Print

faqs.question: Epson Print CD quits unexpectedly when printing from my Mac. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Validate the system's fonts:
Close Epson Print CD and open the
Applications
folder.
Open
Font Book
.
Highlight all of the fonts in the list, then click
File
and
Validate Fonts
.
Remove any corrupted fonts that the software finds and is unable to correct.
Restart your Macintosh, then start Epson Print CD.
If validating the system's fonts does not work, try creating a new user account:
Click the Apple icon, then select
System Preferences
.
Under
System
, select
Accounts
.
If the padlock in the lower left corner is locked, click it to unlock it and enter the password when prompted.
Click the
+
to create a new account.
At the top, change the New Account field to
Administrator
.
Complete the required fields, then click
Create Account
.  (Do not set to automatically log in).
Close the Accounts screen, click on the Apple icon to log out, then log in as the new user.
Open Epson Print CD.
If you are able to use Epson Print CD with the new account but not with the old account, please contact Apple for possible solutions.

faqs.question: What security measures does Epson recommend for its network products?
faqs.answer:
To help deter unauthorized access to your product over a network, you should protect your network environment using appropriate security measures.
Security measures such as these can help deter threats such as loss of user data, use of telephone and fax lines, and other intrusions:
Enable security on your wireless LAN if your product supports a wireless connection
Enable the appropriate security on the wireless LAN you plan to use with your product. Network security, such as a network password, can deter interception of traffic over the wireless LAN. Your router may already have a default password enabled by your Internet service provider (ISP). See your ISP and router documentation for instructions on how to change the default password and better secure your network.
Connect your product only to a network protected by a firewall
Connecting your product directly to the Internet may leave it vulnerable to security threats. Instead, connect it to a router or other networking device protected by a firewall. Your router may already have a firewall set up by your Internet service provider; check with your ISP for confirmation. For best results, set up and use a private IP address for your network connection.
Change the default administrator password on your product
If your product has an option to set an administrator password, change the default administrator password to deter access by unauthorized users to personal data stored on your product, such as IDs, passwords, and contact lists. See the product's User's Guide for more information.
